sections.title: Core Thesis
sections.body: Navier designs and builds software-controlled hydrofoiling vessels in the United States. The same platform that moves people and goods at a fraction of today's cost moves the fight: one core — foils, powertrain, autonomy, fleet software — configured across commercial and defense missions from day one.

sections.render_notes: Invest prose-stage split ONLY: CORE THESIS + thesis_paragraphs verbatim (para 1 lead), thesis-hangar-crane.jpg as right plate (American dynamism — flag visible). Defense bridge body below the split. NO launch film under this chapter — aava/launch film is /invest hero-lightbox only; hangar must appear once.
thesis_paragraphs: The world moves at the speed and cost at which people and goods move. Make a dent in that, and you change how the world works.

Navier builds the vessels and operating infrastructure for high-speed, high-throughput, energy-efficient maritime transportation. Our vessels open new routes; distributed manufacturing scales the fleets; our strategic maritime nodes power and service them — and the network is open to compatible vessels from any manufacturer, all on one standard.

Navier earns recurring revenue on every journey, and every vessel and node added makes the network more valuable. One standardized platform compounding over passenger transport, cargo logistics and defense.

sections.title: Naval Advantage Hinges on Small, Fast, Affordable Platforms.

blocks.head: THE CONNECTOR GAP
blocks.body: Ship-to-shore and littoral movement still runs at displacement speed — the slowest link in every operation.

blocks.head: CREWS ARE THE LIMIT
blocks.body: Planing hulls slam in any real sea. Sea state caps speed; fatigue caps missions.

blocks.head: ONE HULL, ONE MISSION
blocks.body: Every new requirement starts a bespoke program — years to field, a single-mission budget to match.

sections.closer: A standardized foiling platform — stable at speed through Sea State 4, long-range, low-signature, software-defined — changes what a navy can field, and how fast it can field it.

sections.title: The Physics Was Proven in 1969. What Was Missing Was Control.

media.alt: USS Plainview (AGEH-1) foilborne — U.S. Navy experimental hydrofoil, commissioned 1969. U.S. Navy photo.

blocks.head: FLEW IN 1969
blocks.body: 212 ft · 310 tons · 40 knots foilborne — the world's largest hydrofoil

blocks.head: WHY IT RETIRED
blocks.body: Analog control and one-off construction — 268 foilborne hours in its lifetime, never produced at rate

blocks.head: WHAT CHANGED
blocks.body: Software flight control, electric drivetrains, and a production base funded by commercial demand

sections.closer: The physics was proven in 1969. What was missing was control. Control is software now — and software is what Navier builds.

sections.title: Commercial Infrastructure First. Defense on Top.
body: We are a dual-use platform company. Commercial fleets carry the production volume — so defense buys at commercial cost and commercial rate, not bespoke-program cost.

Production capacity exists today across U.S. contract yards — Lyman-Morse (Maine) and Seattle for First-of-Class builds and U.S. programs — with California HQ building NavierOS, foils, and new IP. A flagship U.S. shipyard is planned for 2028, sited for Jones Act and U.S. Navy / NATO production.
Unit cost falls with design and volume, not with spec: the Quanta build is engineered −45% against the first-generation N30, line by line.
